notes.title: Mainland Pawan has Arrived! Update 0.51! Open World!
notes.content:
[h1][b]Update 0.51! Introducing Mainland Pawan![/b][/h1][p] 
[b]After 8 months of development, the latest Expansion Patch for Tormented Soul overhauls the game entirely. Now featuring:[/b][/p][list][*][p][b]9 Skills to level. [/b][/p][/*][*][p][b]Equipment Item levels. [/b](Most equipment rolls a random item power level from 1-100)[/p][/*][*][p][b]All new overhauled soundtrack to fit the new world.  [/b](~40 Songs)[/p][/*][*][p][b]NPC Shops. [/b][/p][/*][*][p][b]Building. [/b](Prefab, instanced base.)[/p][/*][*][p][b]Weather system. [/b][/p][/*][*][p][b]UI overhaul. [/b](Black and red themed, more cohesive.)[/p][/*][*][p][b]Corrupted PvP and Non-PvP zones. [/b][/p][/*][*][p][b]City-teleports [/b][/p][/*][*][p][b]& so much more.[/b] [/p][/*][/list][p][/p][p]This update is more than just a patch — it’s the beginning of an entirely new game. While core systems like [b]combat[/b] and [b]gathering[/b] remain, the old PvP Extraction Arena has been retired to make way for [b]Mainland Pawan[/b], our new Open World mode.[/p][p]Please keep in mind that this mode is still in its early stages and will need a lot more content as development continues. That said, we believe the foundation of our long-term vision is finally in place — and now is the most important time for your feedback. Every idea, suggestion, and critique you share helps shape the future of [i]Tormented Soul[/i].[/p][p]We also want to be upfront: the game may experience [b]future wipes or leagues[/b], as we’re internally leaning toward a league-based progression system/update cycle for items and gear. We want your feedback on this! We may also need to wipe progression for a large balancing overhaul down the line as large content updates occur. We will do our best to avoid future wipes.
[/p][p]We’re incredibly excited about this new direction and can’t wait to hear your thoughts. Join us on [b]Discord[/b] to provide feedback and to help guide what comes next! [/p]

notes.title: Future Plans/Direction & Patch 0.51 Preview
notes.content:
Patch 0.51 is expected to rollout soon—for now here is a sneak peek of what's coming and the future plans beyond.

Behind the scenes—we have made significant improvements to logic that drives our game mode logic and content systems to enable faster content churn & experimentation/iteration throughout the year.

To provide a bit more insight, our original vision was to make a PvPvE-focused open world game that could support up to 100 players. As a 2-person team we chose to first rollout a smaller-scale version Extraction Arena to start with, in order for us to test and learn what we liked about certain systems, playstyles, and mechanics—before expanding scope. Moving forward our goal is to ramp our scope and drive toward assembling all systems needed to achieve our original vision. (Building system, large open-world utilizing our existing PCG systems, combat zones, dynamic game mode systems, etc.) These worlds are planned to allow for 32-100 players in the world at a time, just depending on what we find our systems can support—we utilize thread-safe animations and a variety of techniques to enable us in this area, but performance will be closely monitored for hitches.

In the year ahead we are excited to take risks to bring to you Mainland Pawan, while the Extraction Arena mode benefits from added end-game systems like breaches—coming in patch 0.51. We also look forward to hearing your feedback and suggestions!

notes.title: Patch 0.50 - Mob Overhaul Part 2, RNG+ Expansion, & various improvements!
notes.content:
From both of us at ChainSoul Studio, we wish you all a very Happy Holidays and New Year!

Patch 0.50 is now live - Mob Overhaul Part 2, RNG+ Expansion, & various improvements. This update caps RNG+ at 1000%, but makes RNG+ more attainable with the new Spirit Essence being rewarded from every in-game gatherable/mob/player. RNG+ now factors both corruption & spirit essence. On PvP death, losing items to an enemy player, directly grants you equivalent value for spirit essence and keeps your RNG+ the same. Cleansing items at base also rewards 50% RNG value of spirit essence.

Achieving 1000% bonus RNG in a game is pretty attainable now for any player. One of the core pieces of content players have loved so far, has been the RNG+ system. This update helps us deepen the satisfaction the system provides by reducing the penalty for dying/cleansing. Getting into the late-game with high RNG+ (500%+) and having a crazy amount of loot flowing your way has been insanely fun, and we will keep finding ways to center the game around this unique scaling-loot loop.

This is 100% why the decision to go Early Access was needed for us, we never expected RNG+ to be a central focus of the game's loops. Now we have discovered through player feedback and behavior, it is arguably our most distinctive and satisfying loop in the game currently.

TLDR: Game has RNG+ scaling harder now and it make loot go BRRRR.

Full Patch Notes:
[b]RNG+ Expansion, Backfill ticket improvements, & misc.[/b]
[list]
[*] Added Spirit Essence, which acts as a per-match kept version of RNG scaling.
[*] RNG+ Scaling now factors both your corruption risk and Spirit Essence.
[*] RNG+ is now capped at 1000% RNG.
[*] When dying with corrupt items, users will now be given 100% of the loot value converted to an equivalent rate in Spirit Essence value. (Keep 50% of the RNG+ bonus.)
[*] Cleansed items now convert at a 50% ratio for spirit essence.
[*] Improved mob & player deaths sounds.
[*] Removed a visual cue for character hit reacts that would cause FPS issues in mass-fight situations.
[*] Improved team logic in situations where a player leaves or disconnects to ensure balanced teams on new assignments.
[*] Through debug logging, we discovered 3 corrupt items ID never got made during our corruption dev cycle and have since corrected this—Soul Stones, Torment Stones, and Torment Orbs.

^This would have caused these 3 items to exclusively come from lootcrates, so any players bottlenecked by these materials should now be able to get them much easier.

[*] Removed tips from loadscreens and instead have left them on the rotating tip widget on main menu.

^Loadscreens didn't stay up long enough to load them/read them on most CPUs unfortunately.

[*] Improved backfill logic when players leave a match or disconnect & for ensuring correct Player IDs are linked to backfill tickets for solo party games.
[/list]

[b]NPC Overhaul Specific:[/b]
[list]
[*] Swapped out Wolf boss death animations for now with special FX, similar to tree deaths, due to them being overly buggy. (This is also a trial run of Death VFX to see if we want to go this route.)
[*] All bosses movement speed and Elite movement speed has been increased.
[*] Resolved an AI bug that could cause mobs to stop roaming.
[*] Resolved AI bug for bosses not moving as a result of waiting on previous reset heal logic that had been removed. (Thus stalling out.)
[*] Improved boss chasing logic.
[*] Rebalanced Wyrm boss damage to be more consistent across skill types.
[*] Improved boss strafing/walking logic while attacking & when using certain buff skills where they shouldn't move at all.
[*] Slightly increased boss attack speed with an appropriate offset to damage as a result.
[*] Fixed a future issue regarding boss/npc targeting logic that could have caused crashes in rare scenarios when NPCs fight each other.
[*] In testing team-based mob mass combat we found a few areas to cleanup in the Stats/loot/combat systems. (This effectively was a massive stress test to help us prepare logic for events/breaches/new game modes we are working towards.)

^Many parts of our logic was battle tested & stress tested during mass NPC brawl testing and it exposed a few areas that we have better optimized/cleaned up, so we are super happy with that!

[*] Converted Wyrm mob attack animations to threadsafe for great server/client CPU performance at mass quantity.
[*] Changed mobs homing target to target chest rather than feet, which allows more dodge-ability to certain skills.
[/list]

notes.title: Patch 0.49 - Mob Overhaul Part 1 and various fixes/improvements.
notes.content:
This is part 1 of the Mob Overhaul—we expect a few more updates focused in this area coming soon, but this is a massive improvement over what we previously had.

Shoutout to player: Numbingcactus for finding/reporting an issue with our boss logic! Thank you!

Boss NPC & all NPC changes:
Bosses now chase players within a reasonable distance and feel a lot more intimidating.
Mob reset logic no longer triggers a reset heal, kiting mobs at their reset line is now a fully intended mechanic.
NPC reset logic has been improved for all mobs, now if a reset is triggered a monster will frequently interrupt their migration back toward their spawn point to 'recheck' for players they can hit.
Removed hit animations from bosses for the time being as it was leading to unrealistic boss reactions/bugginess during transition states making bosses move un-naturally. 
After the latest NPC patch the Wyrm hatchlings were doing too much damage, which is now corrected.
Wyrm hatchlings now auto attack using sight within 2.5k meters.
Bosses now auto-attack using sight within 6.5k meters.
Added logic support for Team-based AI logic and etc. behind the scenes which is going to support us heavily going into phase 2.

Other:
Fixed an issue where /show and /hide quick chat commands wouldn't update your current selection.
Added randomized tips to the loading screen along with a 'Loading...' message to ensure it was distinct from the main menu backsplash.
Fixed a bug in scoring logic for a future update where Team-based mobs could be rewarded with stats and cause crashes.

notes.title: Patch 0.47 Improved Processing UI, Elite Ogre improvements, & QOL/Bug fixes.
notes.content:
Shoutout to Carnie - Who reported a few UI bugs and submitted suggestions for improvements.

---Bugs/Performance/VFX improvements/UI improvements---
Added functionality for a craft max quantity into the processing bench by updating the right side display number of the slider to always be the max quantity you can craft. (And its a button also.)
Also capped the 2x functionality on the processing bench to only go to the max quantity you can craft.
^With the above 2 changes, processing should now be much more convenient.
Fixed a display issue on tier 8 enchanted gear showing as roman numeral VII.
Improved peformance on Katana R and Battleaxe R.
Also improved visibility slightly on battleaxe R.
Removed launch vfx on toran's blade E has it was a bit too distracting/bright.
Removed a sound that played when a moon cycle was over, as it felt random and didn't clearly communicate the message it was intended to.
Extended Announcement duration for Ancient Equipment from 4 seconds to 7 seconds.
Improved performance and optimization on several boss projectile VFX.
Fixed cooldowns for previous weapon skills appearing on a quickswapped weapons abilities for a half-second before clearing. (Shoutout to Carnie, it was a very infrequent issue and hard to catch!)
Corrected a very rare issue with weapon icons not switching on quickswap and improved UI network communication regarding advanced ability icon swap logic used for quickswaps.
Corrected another issue that could cause quickswap icons swaps to not show correct cooldowns when the skill wasn't on cooldown.

---Ogre & NPC fixes---
Fixed an ogre spawning with duplicated mesh issue, caused by a change a while back where we improved the animation performance of the ogres.
Added additional ogre spawns & reworked their combat logic to walk more.
Removed ogre ability explosion vfx for the end of their projectile. They now just throw projectiles.
Rebalanced NPC damage to compensate for a previous patch where we buffed health/AP across the board.
Increased respawn rate of ogres.

notes.title: Patch 0.46 - TSR Performance improvements, Native Quality, & DLAA Support.
notes.content:
Added a Native Quality setting into the DLSS/TSR Quality menu for users that want a higher-end quality graphic experience.
We discovered our EPIC TSR (Non-DLSS) settings for new players were defaulting to a native (Max) setting and have now corrected this to default to a balanced option. 
^This results in roughly a 30-40% FPS improvement for new players on average. (Which we are super happy with!!!)

[b]Performance Change Examples that resulted from Balanced Quality TSR over Native Quality TSR (Non-DLSS/DLAA)[/b]
Our developer PCs went from 60-65 FPS on screenspace to 90+ FPS due to the balanced TSR on EPIC settings.
Our developer PCs went from 55 FPS on Lumen to 80+ FPS on EPIC settings, with this change.

notes.title: Early Access Q/A - A very worthwhile read!
notes.content:
[b]Question: "Can I play the game, if there are no other players online? Will I be stuck in queue?"[/b]

You get into a match fast regardless. (~60 seconds or less.) While you play, we are actively backfilling any additional players who queue up to put them in your match. Our game is super early in its community building lifecycle, as we have just entered early access. We have a firm belief that once our game reaches the quality we are building towards, it will naturally attract a large amount of players and grow organically as players tell their friends. We are actively organically marketing on TikTok/YT, but for now this game is largely being forged in the shadows. This provides you with the unique opportunity of being part of a small community giving us feedback early on, and thus having a larger impact on the eventual direction the game heads.

[b]Question: "Why would I want to play solo if no other players are online?"[/b]

Our core game loops work like a Fantasy MMO's progression system. You keep the items you earn game over game and get to progress your gear. So even while playing solo or with a party of friends, our game offers a gear power-grind with over 50 hours of content. And if you are solo, you can enjoy the never-ending scaling grind of risking more and more loot to increase your RNG percent, and gain a significantly faster progression curve then when the playerbase is much larger. (You can reach up to 500%+ rng per game) This is sort of giving you an 'Early-bird' advantage to progression. Just keep an eye on the chat for player join messages—your safety may be temporary. We have already had one player do this for over 15 hours and they are pretty geared, so look out!

[b]Question: "I'm not into PvP, can I still enjoy the grind for gear?"[/b]

We have designed a lot of the game's loops where getting rare drops, hiding behind teammates, & running for your life when needed can be a viable playstyle & even have loadout builds to compliment the playstyle. (Speed/stamina/tank builds.)

[b]Question: "Do you lose everything you have farmed if somebody kills you?"[/b]

Only corrupted loot is lost upon death. When gathering, fighting mobs, or obtaining loot from bosses you receive corrupted loot which can be cleansed by returning to base. The exception to this is Ancient Equipment loot drops which are obtained as cleansed by default, as they are ultra-rare equipment drops. Once cleansed your items are yours to keep. (Until we eventually do our next-season wipe, which is expected every 6 months to 1 year.) There are a variety of ways to return to base such as on your mount or by teleporting, but a few important things to note—Combat/Gathering applies a 3 second dismount debuff and a Block-teleport debuff for 15 seconds. 

[b]Question: "Why risk loot? How is that satisfying when I die?"[/b]

We have an RNG+ corruption scoring system which bonuses your RNG based on the amount of loot you are risking. So even if you gather a bunch of corrupt loot and lose it, you were still gaining a higher chance on each subsequent loot to get an ultra-rare Ancient Equipment pieces. As discussed on our store-page, we incentivize risk to make it rewarding/worth for both sides.

[b]Question: "Why is the core game mode 8v8?"[/b]

We believe this will provide a satisfying team-based feel, where 1 afk teammate won't sink a match and cause you to lose. We are open to reviewing the match sizes to add more players or go with a smaller scale. 

[b]Question: "Can the game handle more players?"[/b]

While we are in the early days, we are trying to limit the game's match sizes to ensure we provide a playable experience with good performance that is reliable for players. From a technical standpoint, every creature/horse/player in our game is using Multi-threaded animations and we are also limiting render distance based on type of entity. (Player, mobs, elites, bosses.) Once our community gets a little larger we will be reviewing and testing possibilities for expanding match sizes or the potential addition of a larger mode. We believe our systems can currently handle 50-100 players in a match performantly, but we want to test it thoroughly before we roll it out.

[b]Question: "Are there microtransactions or in-app purchases?"[/b]

[u]NOPE![/u] All cosmetics are sold through DLC bundles on our Steam page. No pay to win. No pay for convenience. Fair, earned gear-progression only.

[b]Question: "Are there classes?"[/b]

Abilities in the game are tied to weapons that are chosen in your gear loadout. You can swap loadouts mid-match and keep your enchants/regrades in each gear slot! You get 2 weaponsets, with two-hand weapons providing 6 abilities, one-hand weapons providing 4 abilities, and off-hands providing 2 abilities. Total you will have 12 weapon-granted abilities. You will also have a Lightning dash which grants invulnerability for .5 seconds at the cost of 50 stamina. (Great for dodging or gap-closing.)

[b]Question: "Skillshots?"[/b]

Correct, most abilities in the game are skillshots which are aimed via a third-person shooter style of aiming. These are intentionally tooltip-less and fast-paced. Teleports, arrow volleys, tornado summons, some dashes, and projectiles all use this style of aiming. Missing skills against good opponents is common and requires a lot of practice to get good at.

notes.title: Patch 0.45 Improved cave lighting, Biome light variations, & corrupt balancing.
notes.content:

Fixed skybox blur
Updated the Corruption denimator curve from 25k>40k value per 100%. This change is meant to provide a more satisfying corruption RNG+ system grind for the moment, we are actively looking at ways to reward individuals who achieve crazy corruption scores in a match.

With our saga of the lighting rework over the last several patches coming to a close, we are now shifting focus to adding additional content & ramping our marketing efforts.

notes.title: Patch 0.43 Lighting/Character lighting improvements/PCG Forest density increase.
notes.content:
GPU performance improved due to lighting changes.
Updated lighting & graphical sharpness. 
Character lighting in shadowed areas has significantly been improved. 
Sharpness for characters had another minor improvement, carrying on from last patch.
We increased the PCG forest density for the WildernThorn biome, particularly the middle of the map.
We also adjusted the PCG blocking density on mob camps which weren't boss creatures.
We slightly increased the landscape texture brightness for WildernThorn to improve visibility & aesthetic.
We also reduced the server-side spawn radius distance to despawn mobs faster for specifically normal mobs/elites when players are not in range. (This will be handy for larger modes later.)
^The above change builds on previous changes of us preparing for a large mode with far more mobs & a mob overhaul, where we use more multi-threaded humanoid creatures spreadout enough to achieve performance for the server at scale. (Survival-like mode with a hundreds/thousands of mobs.)
Removed grass for now from Wildernthorn & Winter as we didn't feel it was fitting the look we want to achieve.
Adjusted torch light fade-in ranges for WildernThorn cavern & the DiTrine cavern.
Removing team bosses for now, we will be reworking them and reimplementing them in the future.
Removed skybox (moon) for now as it was conflicting with HDRI environment.
This is the last of the art style/lighting change updates (we believe), we are now moving forward into reworking mobs/mechanics/gameplay areas to make the game more fun/challenging.

notes.title: Party bug fixes. Patch 0.37/0.38

This are a smaller patches aimed to fix a few issues remaining after the large patch 0.36—where we added Ancient Equipment & a lot more fixes.

notes.title: Ultra-Rare Ancient Equipment system & a ton of fixes/improvements - Patch 0.36
notes.content:
This is our 4th patch this week, and we didn't hold back!

Patch highlights: 
Added 5 Ancient Equipment slots & 16 Ancient Equipment items with every killable gatherable, mob, boss, and player being able to drop these very rare items. 
Optimized networking code and improved a lot of UI elements.

Full patch notes & some design idea inclusion as we worked to deliver this patch.

Healthbar animation speed increased to prevent skipping the animation on rapid hits. (Toxic ability ticks, rapid-fire bow, etc.)
Improved placement & icons for killfeed.
Fixed an issue where gatherables had a small collision field still active after death.
Dimension Equipment removed for the current game mode
We will be adding a new rare equipment drop system in its place , which will help us be more true to our unique vision. We don't want to provide the player incentive to feel like the game is a race for power—plenty of existing Fantasy MOBAs do that. Our design is aiming more for the feel of a satisfying marathon to obtain gear, with low valleys and high peaks. (This became Ancient Equipment in this patch)
^In response to the Dimension Equipment removal, we have removed vanishing essence for now—we plan to reintroduce the system if we have a core loop fitting its use case need, or in a future game mode.
Improved item toasts text and removed background from it.
Increased environment brightness scattering by a small amount to increase visibility in day and night time.
Added user has joined messages.
Improved text chat look and functionality.
Base health increased by 3,000 to 8,000—this is in preparation for the power players will be obtaining from Ancient Equipment rare drops.
Better saturation blending on grasses that had interesting colors.
Improved collision on gatherables of larger sizes.
Moon cycle now stops at end game, rather than popping right after end-game and teasing players with a bonus drop window.
Flattened rank health rewards a bit more for better balancing.
Ancient Equipment is not corrupted and triggers a DB save immediately when obtained.
Typically quitting a game will cause player's DB to not save their progress which is intended as a penalty for leaving a match—we have added an exception to this on ancient equipment drops as they are very rare.
Added inventory filtering tab for Ancient Equipment.
Swapped out the default lighting from Lumen to Screenspace, Lumen can still be enabled by players, but since it has a high performance cost we want to have it be an option players must turn on.


Net relevancy changes to optimize networking, improve client & server CPU performance, & prepare us for a potential future of high player quant modes & larger maps.
Improved net relevancy code for healthbar—putting higher dependence for accuracy on server updating when net relevance begins.
Scoreboard Stats moved from client side reliance with net relevance being important for tags & states, to a server component.
The above 2 changes allowed us to change our net relevance on NPCs and Players to be more optimized, and when added with a previous change we made a month ago to mesh rendering distances, back in patch 0.24, we are setting ourselves up to not only improve the performance of the game, but for a future where we could potentially offer higher playercounts in gamemodes & larger maps.
We updated our Mob spawner logic to allow us greater developer control, improved PCG blocking, & dynamic optimization of spawn distances based on different types of mobs—allowing us to return humanoid mobs without paying true humanoid skeleton CPU prices.

notes.title: Matchmaking Overhaul Part 2 - 0.35 All matches now backfill additional players.
notes.content:
This update continues forward from Matchmaking Overhaul Part 1, where we added matchmade game backfilling support (Adding more players to your game as you play.) and a critical rare connection issue. 

This update adds Solo Match backfilling. Now any match in game that is not full, will be actively searching for additional players to add to the game. This is a dramatic shift from where we were just a few days ago.

[b]What does this actually mean?[/b]

We have reduced matchmaking time to 60 seconds. You get in a solo match within 60 seconds if no other matches are found to be active with empty slots. As you play, we are actively matchmaking for additional players to add to your game. 

This reduces the time spent staring at the menu. Eliminates the split match problem we previously had if people queued up after a match had just started—and should allow us to deliver a far more exciting experience while we are in the early days of Early Access. 

Thank you all for your patience and can't wait to compete against, and compete with, you all in game! ːsteamhappyː

notes.title: Matchmaking Overhaul Part 1 - 0.34
notes.content:
This update adds support for backfilling in progress matches that were successfully matchmade between 2 parties, where new matchmaking tickets will be directed to your game until it is full. In the next update, we hope to add a workaround for solo games to take advantage of similar logic. 

Our previous logic relied on keeping guardrails on to try to get a match as full as possible, now our systems are completely reversed. Two parties or individual players searching for a match can find a match within 20-30 seconds, and we backfill additional players in as they play. Which should hopefully lead to players bunching into cycles of searching around the same time—which will help dramatically while we are in the early days of early access.

Most of our systems work great under this new design of join-in-progress, but we are looking to change Dimension Equipment in a future update—potentially transitioning it into a rare equipment drop system. We want bigger moments of "wow, I can't believe I got that", so regardless of how we get there, expect that to be a priority.

We have reduced the time to enter a solo match from 4 minutes in Queue to 2 minutes and 30 seconds. 

We are not done improving this area of eliminating time spent staring at our menu, and we hope to make it even better in the next update. Thank you all for your patience and hope to see you all in game!

This update also adds a permanent fix for a root cause of failed connections mentioned in the previous patch & has other various bug fixes primarily with matchmaking UI feedback.

notes.title: Patch 0.33
notes.content:
Homebase VFX sizing corrected.
Added base area UI messages to inform the player their abilities won't damage if casted in base, & to warn them of enemy base tick-damage.
Added multi-attempt joining incase the first attempt to join fails. (This occurred rarely, about 1 in 15 games and now should be dramatically less.)
Fixed a weapon regrading issue with mainhand/offhand logic.

notes.title: Early Access—November 15th! A Sneak Peek at Day 1.
notes.content:
At the start of early access—There are 18 weapons with 72 different abilities, 92 armor & gem pieces, 18 Torments & Souls, 10 enchant tiers & 5 regrade tiers respectively to progress through on loadout gear & weapons, 3 different biomes with 2 additional sub-biomes, 16 different bosses (4 boss types with 4 variations each), 51 Ranks, 30 craftable buffs, 18 different pieces of Dimension equipment (Temporary per-game gear.), & over 180 unique items to obtain.

Our combat system provides fast movement, vertical freedom on abilities, third-person shooter aiming with projectiles, & fantasy action combat in one intuitive bundle. The horse mount has 3 abilities with the Sprint, Glide, & Leap offering great movement when not in combat. Our respawn timers are consistently 8 seconds. Never waste 40-70 seconds staring at a screen again. Zoom out of base with your horse abilities and an additional 'base defender' movement speed buff every time. Nearly every skill in the game is an AOE which means no more mageballing—every weapon is viable in group fights. Tired of small abilities in a fantasy combat system? Good. We didn't hold back—ready to bring down 5 enemies with one combo? We embrace freedom of choice, and haven't assigned you a lane or role. The map is full of resources to progress your gear. Work with your team, or hunt down enemies on your own. The choice of what to prioritize and how to play is up to you.

We are thrilled to dive into the world of Pawan with you all in a little under 2 weeks!
